recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. The current build source satisfies the published FHIR-19590 decision; any future cleanup of historical/internal binding labels should be handled as a separate work-group decision rather than as required FHIR-19590 reconciliation.
issue_request: FHIR-19590 is a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Device change request asking to rename the former FHIR Device Type / device-kind value set to Device Type so other specifications could reference it. The recorded resolution says Device and DeviceDefinition should reference http://hl7.org/fhir/valueset-device-type.html, with DeviceDefinition being the source needing change.
initial_application: The change was applied by existing history: a8227bb51b renamed source/device/valueset-device-kind.xml to source/device/valueset-device-type.xml and changed the Device binding name to DeviceType; 90089e6daa corrected the value set name/title to DeviceType / Device Type; 902dde180b updated DeviceDefinition to bind to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/device-type; and 3a62519d7f removed remaining old active source references.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists both device and devicedefinition as active current resources. The current source has no active device-kind or valueset-device-kind references outside historical release snapshots. The July 2019 OO Confluence minutes include FHIR-19590 in Device block-vote material. A later Zulip thread about Device type versus kind raised terminology clarity concerns but did not reverse the canonical rename. FHIR-19588 was co-applied in a8227bb51b but concerns DeviceDefinition.safety and is already represented on the combined branch; FHIR-16125 is an earlier no-change DeviceKind expansion question.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/device/valueset-device-type.xml has url http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/device-type and title Device Type, and the active Device.type and DeviceDefinition.classification.type definitions bind to that value set. A remaining DeviceKind bindingName label on DeviceDefinition.classification.type is not the canonical value set URL/title targeted by this Jira and does not change the requested conformance target.
